  "single_defensible_answer": true,
  "source_support": true,
  "numeric_solution": false,
  "boundary_cases": true,
  "passage_integrity": true,
  "passage_answerability": true,
  "meaningfully_distinct": true,
  "evidence_ids": ["E3.1"],
  "reasons": [
    "Under a fixed exchange rate system, an official government action that increases the exchange rate (making the domestic currency cheaper in terms of foreign currency) is defined by NCERT as devaluation."
  ],
  "syllabus_chapter": "Balance of Payments",
  "syllabus_topic": "Foreign exchange rate - fixed and flexible exchange rates, devaluation and revaluation",
  "syllabus_entitlement": true,
  "presentation_ready": true,
  "question_type_match": true,
  "principle_applicability": "excerpt_required",
  "decisive_principle_in_excerpts": true,
  "answer_conditions": [
    {
      "condition": "The exchange rate regime is a fixed exchange rate system.",
      "status": "explicit",
      "alters_key_if_changed": true,
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    },
    {
      "condition": "The official exchange rate is increased by the government from Rs 75 to Rs 80 per dollar.",
      "status": "explicit",
      "alters_key_if_changed": true,
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    },
    {
      "condition": "Under NCERT definitions, an official increase in the exchange rate under a fixed regime is devaluation.",
      "status": "convention",
      "alters_key_if_changed": true,
      "convention_evidence_ids": ["E3.1"]
    }
  ],
  "option_challenges": [
    {
      "option": "A",
      "strongest_reading": "Revaluation occurs if the government decreases the exchange rate making domestic currency costlier, which is not the case here.",
      "correct_under_reading": false,
      "reading_status": "contradicts_stem",
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    },
    {
      "option": "C",
      "strongest_reading": "Appreciation refers to a rise in currency value determined by market forces in a flexible exchange rate regime.",
      "correct_under_reading": false,
      "reading_status": "contradicts_stem",
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    },
    {
      "option": "D",
      "strongest_reading": "Floating refers to market-determined exchange rates without fixed pegging, not a peg adjustment.",
      "correct_under_reading": false,
      "reading_status": "contradicts_stem",
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    }
  ],
  "blocking_defects": [],
  "style_notes": [],
  "cuet_fit": {
    "criteria": {
      "syllabus_objective": {
        "level": 3,
        "evidence": "Directly tests the core distinction between devaluation and revaluation in a fixed exchange rate regime."
      },
      "format_authenticity": {
        "level": 3,
        "evidence": "Standard four-option conceptual MCQ directly mapped to NCERT definitions."
      },
      "level_calibration": {
        "level": 3,
        "evidence": "Direct recall and conceptual comprehension typical of CUET UG Economics questions."
      },
      "discrimination_value": {
        "level": 3,
        "evidence": "Effectively tests candidate confusion between depreciation/appreciation vs devaluation/revaluation."
      }
    },
    "reasoning_steps": 1,
    "estimated_difficulty": "easy",
    "cognitive_level": "recall",
    "exemplar_ids_compared": []
  },
  "option_resolution": [
    {
      "option": "A",
      "status": "contradicted",
      "false_part": "Revaluation",
      "premise_source": "excerpt",
      "evidence_id": "E3.1",
      "premise_quote": "On the other hand, a Revaluation is said to occur, when the Government decreases the exchange rate (thereby, making domestic currency costlier) in a fixed exchange rate system.",
      "reason": "Revaluation decreases the exchange rate, whereas here the rate increased from 75 to 80."
    },
    {
      "option": "B",
      "status": "supported",
      "false_part": "",
      "premise_source": "excerpt",
      "evidence_id": "E3.1",
      "premise_quote": "In a fixed exchange rate system, when some government action increases the exchange rate (thereby, making domestic currency cheaper) is called Devaluation.",
      "reason": "Increasing the price of dollars from 75 to 80 rupees under a fixed regime is devaluation."
    },
    {
      "option": "C",
      "status": "contradicted",
      "false_part": "Appreciation of the rupee",
      "premise_source": "excerpt",
      "evidence_id": "E2.1",
      "premise_quote": "Similarly, in a flexible exchange rate regime, when the price of domestic currency (rupees) in terms of foreign currency (dollars) increases, it is called Appreciation of the domestic currency (rupees) in terms of foreign currency (dollars).",
      "reason": "Appreciation belongs to flexible regimes and represents a strengthening domestic currency."
    },
    {
      "option": "D",
      "status": "contradicted",
      "false_part": "Floating of the exchange rate",
      "premise_source": "excerpt",
      "evidence_id": "E1.1",
      "premise_quote": "This exchange rate is determined by the market forces of demand and supply. It is also known as Floating Exchange Rate .",
      "reason": "The system remains fixed; the peg was adjusted by government action."
    }
  ]
}
